7.2 Citation

Reference links should appear at least at first mention and spell out what the reference refers to in the first occurrence.

Bad: discussed in [XMLName]. Better: discussed in Namespaces in XML [XMLName].

7.3 Citing a Reference From Within a Document

When linking to an external resource from body prose, indicate you are leaving the document and after the link cite the entry in references section with section/page detail where useful.

11. Editorial Guidelines

Use U.S. English spelling; avoid repeated words; ensure subject-verb agreement; break long sentences; avoid "click here" link text; use specific W3C "this version" URIs where intended; visible URI and href should match.

13. Commonly Misspelled Terms

  • JavaScript (cap S)
  • homepage/home page allowed
  • website preferred one word
  • read-only hyphenate
  • webpage/web page allowed
  • URIs not URI's
  • DTDs not DTD's
  • line feed two words
  • lowercase and uppercase one word
  • worldwide one word
  • World Wide Web three words
